Pioneer of Faith
PY-uh-neer uhv FAYTH
proper noun
A title of Christ as the trail-blazing Captain and Author of faith and salvation (Hebrews 2:10; 12:2); the One who leads the way to glory.

Biblical Definition

Pioneer of faith is a title of Christ drawn from the epistle to the Hebrews, where He is called the author and finisher of our faith and the captain of our salvation—the trail-blazer who goes before His people, opening the way to God and leading the way to glory. He is the author of faith, the One in whom faith begins and on whom it fixes its eye, who for the joy that was set before Him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God; and He is its finisher, who perfects the faith He begins. It became the Father, in bringing many sons unto glory, to make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings—the Pioneer made complete as Saviour through the very road of suffering He traveled before His people. He is the forerunner entered for us within the veil, the High Priest after the order of Melchizedek; being made perfect, He became the author of eternal salvation unto all them that obey Him. The dictionary reads the Pioneer of faith as Christ the trail-blazing Captain: the One who, as the eternal Son made man, ran the race of faith before us, blazed the path through suffering and death into glory, entered heaven as our forerunner, and now leads His many sons along the way He opened, perfecting the faith He authored until they are with Him where He is.

Webster 1828 Definition

A title of Christ as the trail-blazing Captain and Author of faith and salvation; who ran the race before us, opened the way through suffering to glory, and entered as our forerunner.

PIONEER OF FAITH, Christ the trail-blazing Author and Captain of faith and salvation.

The author and finisher of our faith, who endured the cross for the joy set before Him (Heb 12:2).

The captain of salvation made perfect through sufferings (Heb 2:10).

Key Scripture

Heb 12:2 — "Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God."

Heb 2:10 — "For it became him, for whom are all things, and by whom are all things, in bringing many sons unto glory, to make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings."

Heb 6:20 — "Whither the forerunner is for us entered, even Jesus, made an high priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec."

Heb 5:9 — "And being made perfect, he became the author of eternal salvation unto all them that obey him;"

Modern Corruption

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition, though “pioneer” may be misread to make Christ a mere example to imitate; He is the Captain who accomplishes the salvation He pioneers.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The misreading to guard against is the reduction of Christ the Pioneer to a mere moral example—the first and best man of faith whom we are simply to imitate—as though His pioneering were only an inspiring precedent and not an accomplishing work. But the Captain of salvation does not merely show the way; He opens it and brings His people through it. He is the author of our faith, not only its model; the captain who secures the victory, not only its herald; the forerunner who has entered within the veil to bring us after Him. He saves those He leads; He does not merely encourage them.

The principle to recover is Christ as the trail-blazing Captain who accomplishes salvation. As the eternal Son made man He ran the race of faith before us, endured the cross for the joy set before Him, and was made perfect as Saviour through the very sufferings He bore in our place; He entered heaven as our forerunner and High Priest. He is the author of faith and its finisher, beginning and perfecting it in His people. We look unto Jesus not merely to copy Him but to be carried by Him—the Pioneer who blazed the path and leads His many sons home to glory.
